items.followUp: Differentiate between packet header and packet payload.

rubric.why: The payload is the content being sent.
rubric.description: Identifies payload as the actual message or data being transmitted.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the payload as the message or data being sent.

rubric.why: Control information helps manage the delivery of the payload.
rubric.description: Identifies control information as information used to manage or direct delivery.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating a purpose such as addressing, routing, or managing delivery.

modelAnswer: Payload is the actual message or data being transmitted.
Control information contains details, such as addressing or routing information, that help deliver the payload.

items.followUp: What is a web hosting service?

rubric.why: ISP stands for Internet Service Provider.
rubric.description: Gives the full form of ISP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct expansion.

rubric.why: An ISP gives its users a connection to the Internet.
rubric.description: Describes the service provided by an ISP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it provides Internet access or a connection.

modelAnswer: ISP stands for Internet Service Provider.
It is an organization that provides users with access to the Internet.

items.followUp: What do the HTML attributes rowspan and colspan specify?

rubric.why: Colspan specifies how many columns a table cell spans.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that colspan merges or spans columns.

rubric.why: Rowspan specifies how many rows a table cell spans.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that rowspan merges or spans rows.

modelAnswer: The colspan attribute specifies the number of columns a table cell spans.
The rowspan attribute specifies the number of rows a table cell spans.

items.followUp: Explain how encryption protects an online payment.

rubric.why: Encryption changes readable information into a protected form.
rubric.description: Explains that encryption converts readable data into an unreadable form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the conversion to ciphertext or otherwise unreadable data.

rubric.why: Encryption helps prevent unauthorized people from reading sensitive information.
rubric.description: States that encryption protects data from unauthorized access or protects privacy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying this protection.

rubric.why: Encryption helps keep sensitive information safe during online activities.
rubric.description: Gives an everyday Internet use that encryption protects.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example, such as online transactions or banking.

rubric.why: The protected data can be read by an authorized user after decryption.
rubric.description: Mentions authorized decryption or the key needed to read the data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that an authorized user can decrypt the information, typically using a key.

modelAnswer: Encryption converts readable information (plaintext) into an unreadable form (ciphertext).
It helps prevent unauthorized people from reading sensitive information and protects privacy.
It is important for everyday Internet activities such as online banking and shopping because it protects payment and personal details.
An authorized user can convert the information back by decrypting it with the appropriate key.

items.followUp: Explain the abstraction rule in problem solving.

rubric.why: The rule begins by breaking a complex problem into simpler parts.
rubric.description: States that a large or complex problem is divided into smaller parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the division into smaller, manageable sub-problems.

rubric.why: The smaller problems are solved and their solutions contribute to solving the original problem.
rubric.description: Explains what is done with the smaller parts or their solutions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the parts are solved and their solutions are combined or used to solve the main problem.

modelAnswer: The Divide and Conquer Rule breaks a complex problem into smaller, manageable sub-problems.
Each sub-problem is solved, and the solutions are combined to solve the original problem.

items.followUp: What is data validation, and how does it differ from verification?

rubric.why: Verification checks entered or copied data against its source.
rubric.description: States that verification involves checking data against the original source.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning comparison with the original data or source.

rubric.why: Comparison or checking methods are used to detect copying or entry errors.
rubric.description: Gives a method or purpose of verification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable method, such as double entry or visual checking, or for stating that it checks accuracy.

modelAnswer: Verification is done by checking entered data against the original source.
It can be carried out by visual checking or by entering the data twice and comparing the entries.

items.followUp: What is missing data in a dataset?

rubric.why: Absent data refers to a value that is missing from a dataset.
rubric.description: Identifies absent data as missing or not-present data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the data or value is missing or not present.

rubric.why: The missing value belongs to a field or record in the dataset.
rubric.description: Locates the absent data within a dataset.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating the missing value to a field, record, or dataset.

modelAnswer: Absent data is a value that is missing or not present for a particular field or record in a dataset.

items.followUp: Name two attributes of the HTML <font> tag and state what they control.

rubric.why: The font tag is used to change the appearance of text.
rubric.description: Identifies the purpose of the <font> tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it changes or specifies the appearance of text.

rubric.why: These attributes specify the typeface, size, or colour of the text.
rubric.description: Names an attribute controlled by the font tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a relevant attribute, such as face, size, or color.

modelAnswer: The <font> tag is used to change the appearance of text on a web page.
Its face, size, and color attributes specify the typeface, text size, and text color.
